guitar.notes: Chuck Berry was a guitarist himself, famously associated with the Gibson ES-350T (and later ES-355) — foundational rock'n'roll guitar imagery.

tone.summary: A classic 50s rockabilly tone achieved using a light OD boost into a Fender-style amp model (US Deluxe) with minimal reverb and chorus for space.

rig.name: Chuck Berry - Rock And Roll Music - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise from the guitar signal.
Provide the light edge-of-breakup grit and boost for sharp pick attack.

alternatives.reason: Slightly more aggressive, but Green OD is better for vintage twang.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean, bright sound of a Tweed Fender combo.

alternatives.reason: Also good for vintage sounds, but US Deluxe captures the specific 'Tweed' character better.

blocks.purpose: Match the bright, articulate sound of a small combo speaker.
Enhance the bright twang and single-note clarity.
Bypass (No wah needed for this style).
Add subtle width and movement without sounding ambient.
blocks.gap: The prompt avoids modulation, but a very light Chorus adds necessary 'space' for the rockabilly feel without being distracting.

alternatives.reason: Too rhythmic and noticeable; Chorus is subtler.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required light slapback echo effect.
Add minimal natural room ambience without sounding ambient or muddy.
blocks.gap: The prompt avoids 'ambient reverb,' but a very low-mix Room setting is necessary to give the tone depth and prevent it from sounding too dry/sterile.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default IR for a vintage Fender-style speaker that better captures the Telecaster/Tweed sound.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Vintage Tweed 4x10 or US Deluxe 2x12 (specific IR)
proposals.reason: The current IR is generic; a specific vintage Fender cabinet will enhance the required Telecaster/Tweed character.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased authenticity and clarity in the high end.
